pr_title: statistics: add schema ID to check if it is a system or mem table
pr_body:
<!--

Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/52040

Problem Summary:

During the upgrade process, if there are two different TiDB versions running in the same cluster, statistics will be created for system tables. For example, if we upgrade from v7.5.0 to v8.0.0, and the newer version has a table called `mysql.request_unit_by_group` that was not present in the previous version, we will accidentally create statistics for this newly added table. However, we should avoid creating any statistics for system tables.

### What changed and how does it work?

Ignore all system table DDL events from the DDL handler.

I put in a lot of effort to test this patch during the upgrade process, but it was quite challenging to do so. This issue only arises when two different versions of TiDB are present in the cluster, with the older version serving as the DDL worker. Therefore, it's difficult to trigger this bug. Furthermore, this PR cannot be easily cherry-picked to the older version, as we made significant changes to the DDL handling. Therefore, we can only use unit tests to cover it.

Documentation

### Release note

<!-- compatibility change, improvement, bugfix, and new feature need a release note -->

Please refer to [Release Notes Language Style Guide](https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/release-notes-style-guide.html) to write a quality release note.

```release-note

Fixed an issue where TiDB would create statistics for system tables during upgrades
```

comments:
It is not a bug. From the [documents](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/dev/sql-faq#whats-the-trigger-strategy-for-auto-analyze-in-tidb), we will know that 

When the number of rows in a table or a single partition of a partitioned table reaches 1000, and the ratio (the number of modified rows / the current total number of rows) of the table or partition is larger than [tidb_auto_analyze_ratio](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/dev/system-variables#tidb_auto_analyze_ratio), the [ANALYZE](https://docs.pingcap.com/tidb/dev/sql-statement-analyze-table) statement is automatically triggered.

so it has no stats but the stats meta will still exist to use in many scenarios.

I think this is a bug. Because in the auto-analyze we will skip mem and system tables.

https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/985d7dad7f78ec4b30223b7c3dafb7cee0caea5d/pkg/statistics/handle/autoanalyze/refresher/refresher.go#L179

I guess the issue comes from the show stats_healthy statement which doesn't consider the system table.
This issue is caused by the data import process, we shouldn't update the meta of system tables.

review_comments: If the schema name in DDL jobs is always available, we should use it to simplify our code.
